utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

chapters.summary: Norberto Briceño, a NYC content creator focused on art, history, and infrastructure, says he has made videos about the Mamdani administration's work on faster buses but was never paid, arguing content creators help the city reach people who do not get news from traditional outlets, while paid relationships should be transparent.
chapters.title: Norberto Briceño says he makes unpaid videos about city government

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon and thank you for the opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: My name is Norberto Briseño.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I'm a New York City content creator and my work focuses on art, history, infrastructure, and the kind of interesting things about the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I want to start by being completely transparent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I have made videos about the Momdani administration, usually talking about their work in making buses faster.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I have never been paid by the administration to make those videos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I've done them because I think it's useful for my audience and residents in general to know what their local government is doing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: And I think there's an important conversation to have about that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: There are more than 8 million people in this city, and they don't all get their information from the same place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Some people read newspapers or watch local news.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Others get their information from cable networks, and others get their information from social media.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: No single outlet can reach everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: That's why I think content creators can play an important role in helping the city communicate with the public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: My work is already about New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: So when I talk about what our elected officials are doing, it's because it connects to the things that I cover and the questions my audience cares about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Journalists, media outlets, and creators can all play different roles in making sure that New Yorkers have access to accurate, factual information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: And communication with the government doesn't have to mean agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Ultimately, people should have the opportunity to hear what their government is doing and make up their own minds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Of course, when the city pays a creator to produce something, that relationship should be transparent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: But simply communicating with creators shouldn't be treated as inherently political or improper.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: We live in a social media age, and if the local government wants New Yorkers to understand what's happening in their city, they have to meet them where they are.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: An informed New Yorker is better equipped to participate and hold the government accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: So I think that's good for New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: So thank you.

chapters.summary: Brewer asks Briceño whether he received guidance on avoiding political content after transitioning from campaign to government communications; Briceño says he has media training and focuses on straight facts without swaying the audience, and believes other content creators do the same.
chapters.title: Brewer asks Briceño about guidance on staying non-political

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And so when you were also part of the group of people who were participating in the campaign and then you switched over, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And you were, were you given, I would say, guidance on how to be not political when you're part of a government?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: listserv, so to speak, or it was just known that that's how you have to be?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: No, I think I've had experience in media training, and so for the most part, I never, what I tend to focus on is literally the straight facts, and literally, you know, I don't try to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: sway the audience to think one way or another.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I just literally say the facts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: What are people talking about?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: And as my content is usually very dry because it keeps to the fact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And you find that that's true with some of the other content folks also, is it keeping to the facts?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: From what I've seen and what I've connected with.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Norberto Briceño
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Brewer calls Chris Johnson in person and Tim Fulton online as the next witnesses.
chapters.title: Brewer calls Christopher Leon Johnson and online witness Tim Fullerton

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We'll have Chris Johnson in person, and then online we're going to have Tim Fulton.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Ready?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Yes.

chapters.summary: Christopher Leon Johnson, a press credential holder, accuses Mr. Fingers and Uptown Voices of being paid through third-party agencies, says mayor's offices control the narrative and make creators delete videos, and argues the administration relies on influencers instead of real journalism.
chapters.title: Christopher Leon Johnson accuses influencers of being paid through third-party vendors

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Yeah, my name is Christopher Leon Johnson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I'm a media press credential holder, 47360 as far as 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Let me make this clear that both Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Fingers and Uptown Voices are known liars.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Let me make this clear that they get paid through third-party agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: That's how they get paid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: The way it works in mayor's offices, they control the narrative.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: If you ask a mayor a question they don't want to hear, they will not allow it to be asked to the point where they'll make you delete the videos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Let me make this clear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: These guys are getting paid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: They won't admit it because if they start admitting to the people that they're getting paid, they lose all credibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: They get paid through third-party vendors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Let's keep that clear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I want to say this right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: The problem with this mayor administration is that they solely rely on influencers, and he doesn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Room 9 controls City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Room 9 is the reason why he's the mayor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: They can easily turn on this guy and say, like, well, let's give him the Eric Adams heat, Andrew Cuomo heat, and he's

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: out of here as mayor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: But what needs to start going forward is that people like Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Fingers need to be transparent to his people and tell them that he will never hold the mayor accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: I think that Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Fingers is Mayor McDonough's little go-to Negro when it comes to pushing the narrative for the mayor's administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: That's the facts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: You know, the problem with the city is that this mayor administration, this is an influencer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Relied on administration instead of like real journalism and real journalism starts at room nine not with these fake influencers that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: just hold an iPhone thinking that they know stuff about the city because they do little little little kiddie type tick-tock videos

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: going forward I think the city council needs to really should ask mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Fingers but everybody knew why he was busy because he didn't want to answer the hard questions that well how do you get yeah do you work with the third-party vendors that the city

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: hires to do the content with.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: So going forward, thank you for having us here, Mrs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: And that's all I got to say.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: But yeah, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Fingers is my Donnie's go-to Negro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Leon Johnson
utterances.text: Take care.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Online, we've got Tim Fullerton.

chapters.summary: Tim Fullerton, founder of Find Out Media and former chief digital officer of New York State and Obama administration digital strategist, says Signal group members were not paid by the Mamdani administration or a third party, criticizes the New York Post's coverage of Rowland, and calls the Signal group a distribution list giving the same information as the press.
chapters.title: Tim Fullerton defends Signal group as a distribution list and rebuts accusations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: I have a prepared statement, but I do want to make something very clear based on the previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: The people in that group were not paid by the Memdani administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: They were not paid by a third party.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: That is a signal chat that gets them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: the same type of information that Room 9 gets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: I will also say something about Room 9.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: The New York Post, when they covered this story, ran a photo of Emilia Rowland in it, which was something that they pulled from her Instagram account, and it was a photo of her in a swimming pool.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: So if we're going to talk about credibility and we're going to talk about who has the credibility,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: There is plenty of blame to go around with people who are good actors and who are not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: And the New York Post decided to go down a sexist route to try to make a salacious point because they didn't have any details or any specifics about what this was, nor they understood it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: So I just want to respond to that outrageous comment that was made before and was highly inappropriate for a million reasons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: And again, they may get paid by a third-party entity for creator work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: They did not get that from the Memdani administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: So I just want to clear the record there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Moving on to my statement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: So as I said, my name is Tim Fullerton.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: I'm the founder and CEO of Find Out Media, which is a left-leaning progressive media operation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: I have also been the chief digital officer of the state of New York, and I've also been the director of digital strategy in the Obama administration at the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Department of the Interior, so I know a little bit about this issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: And I want to thank Chair Brewer and the members of the committee for having me today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: And I want to talk a little bit about what happened here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: You know, when I did these jobs in the federal government and the state government, I learned

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: something simple.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Government information is only useful if it reaches people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Today, millions of New Yorkers don't get their news from newspapers or the six o'clock broadcast, or frankly, even know it exists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: They get it from creators they trust on platforms that they already use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: A mayor's office that ignores those people isn't being careful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: It's being absent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: So let's be clear about what this signal group is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: It's a distribution list.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: The mayor's office...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Event invitations and access to officials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: This is the same thing that the press gets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: Now, I believe that the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: They need to turn on, and they have turned on, the thing that keeps them from being deleted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: But this is the same information that the press is getting, and I think it would be wise for the city council to look at this and modify some rules to make sure that all types of communication are

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tim Fullerton
utterances.text: allowed so that the mayor can get his information out, especially in areas where the press isn't covering.

summary: The Committee on Governmental Operations, State & Federal Legislation held an oversight hearing on 'Access to City Government and the Mamdani Administration's Civic Engagement Efforts,' examining the mayor's use of social media influencers and an invite-only Signal group chat.

Agency testimony from DORIS, the Office of Mass Engagement, and the Campaign Finance Board revealed gaps in records retention rules for instant messaging, unclear influencer disclosure standards, and that the Communications office—which oversees the influencer program—declined to appear.

Four preconsidered bills were discussed: prohibiting candidates in government-funded communications during campaigns, reporting on third-party public communications, disclosure requirements for government-funded communications, and campaign finance disclosures for online content; the CFB raised concerns about several as drafted.
